chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudaylah ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Regarding a woman who was unaware that she had not thrown the Jamarat until she returned to Mecca, he said: She should return and throw the Jamarat as she had been throwing them, and the man is the same.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: The Jamarat, the pillars or stone-markers in Mina where pilgrims throw stones during Hajj
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca, the holy city where the rituals of Hajj take place

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to throw the Jamarat until after leaving Mecca?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) regarding the specific case of forgetting to throw the Jamarat until after departing Mecca, mandating a return to the site to complete the missed pillar. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the completeness of Hajj rituals, distinguishing it from other schools that may allow compensation elsewhere or later. The equal application to men and women underscores the universal nature of this obligation within the ritual framework.
